gloss: to lean forward, to embark on

definitions.explanation: To move the upper body forward, showing interest or eagerness.

definitions.gloss: to embark on, to venture into
definitions.explanation: To start participating in or launching into a new activity or field.

examples.japanese: {身|み}を{乗|の}り{出|だ}して{話|はなし}を{聞|き}いた。
examples.english: I leaned forward and listened to the story.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{事業|じぎょう}に{乗|の}り{出|だ}す。
examples.english: To venture into a new business.

examples.japanese: {政府|せいふ}が{対策|たいさく}に{乗|の}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The government has embarked on countermeasures.

notes:
{乗|の}り{出|だ}す is a compound verb with two main meanings: physically leaning forward, or figuratively embarking on something.

COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
{乗|の}る (to ride) + {出|だ}す (to start/put out)

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {身|み}を{乗|の}り{出|だ}す: to lean forward (showing interest)
- {事業|じぎょう}に{乗|の}り{出|だ}す: to venture into a business
- {対策|たいさく}に{乗|の}り{出|だ}す: to take action on measures
- {海外|かいがい}に{乗|の}り{出|だ}す: to expand overseas

NUANCE:
Sense 2 (embark on) often implies taking initiative or actively getting involved in something new.
